rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when something becomes different or turns into something else.

example.english: The weather is starting to change and get cold.
example.jyutping: tin1 hei3 hoi1 ci2 bin3 dung3 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a process or result of becoming different.

example.english: There has been a lot of change in this job.
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 gung1 jau5 hou2 do1 bin3 faa3

rows.note: Use this for small denominations or loose cash, including coins, rather than money returned after a purchase.

example.english: I carry some change when I go out.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ceot1 gaai1 wui5 daai3 ding6 di1 saan2 zi2

rows.note: Use this when someone deliberately makes or alters something into a different form.

example.english: I want to change the design.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 goi2 go3 cit3 gai3

rows.note: Use this for replacing one thing with another, including changing clothes when the context makes that clear.

example.english: I want to change my phone.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 wun6 bou6 din6 waa2

rows.note: Use this specifically for the money returned when the amount paid exceeds the price.

example.english: I paid fifty dollars and got twenty dollars in change.
example.traditional: 我畀五十蚊，收返二十蚊找續。
example.jyutping: ngo5 bei2 ng5 sap6 man1 sau1 faan1 ji6 sap6 man1 zaau2 zuk6

rows.note: Use this nominally for a transfer between vehicles during a journey.

example.english: We need to change trains at Prince Edward to get to Mong Kok.
example.jyutping: heoi3 wong6 gok3 jiu3 hai2 taai3 zi2 zyun2 ce1

rows.note: Use this specifically when transferring from one train, bus, or other vehicle to another.

example.english: To get to Sha Tin, you have to change trains at Kowloon Tong.
example.traditional: 去沙田要喺九龍塘轉車。
example.jyutping: heoi3 saa1 tin4 jiu3 hai2 gau2 lung4 tong4 zyun2 ce1
